newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Fahey doubts room for rate cut.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Fahey doubts room for rate cut.

text.p: Australian Finance Minister John Fahey said on Thursday he doubted there was room for another reduction in official interest rates.

"The governor of the Reserve Bank sees an upward movement in wages as the most significant factor in interest rate rises," Fahey said when asked about data showing a rise in average weekly earnings. "I still think we are in an area where we shouldn't see in any shape or form any increase in interest rates," he said. "Whether there is room as a result of this small upward movement (in wages), for a futher reduction, I think that's very much in doubt."

"We've got inflation down. We've got savings increasing through government initiatives and we need to have moderate wage growth," Fahey told reporters after leaving a Property Council of Australia business meeting.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics on Thursday released average weekly earnings data for the March quarter which showed an overall rise of 1.0 percent taking annual wage growth to 4.3 percent from 3.9 percent in the December quarter.
Private sector wage growth was a stronger than expected 1.3 percent taking annual growth to 3.6 percent from 2.8 percent.

The Reserve Bank, which tracks wages growth as part of its strategy of meeting the 2-3 percent underlying inflation target, last changed monetary policy in December when it cut the official cash rate by 50 basis points to 6.0 percent.
This was the central bank's third cut by the same amount since mid-1996.
